✍️ Gaming Industry Trends & Market Insights

Beyond IP Brand Power: 'Operational Sincerity' and the Reshaping of the Fandom Economy

In an era where fandom is capital, why do some make a brilliant comeback while others fade behind the scenes? 🎮 The data-proven turnaround of small developers and the exit of massive IPs suggest that the survival laws of the game industry have changed.
While Epid Games' 'Trickcal Re:vive' achieved a miracle for small developers with 46.8 billion KRW in annual revenue, 'Link! Like! Love Live!', which boasted a powerful fandom, announced its service termination. Simultaneously, Netmarble is attempting to extend the lifespan of its IP by reinterpreting past glory with a modern touch through the 'MONSTERS Taming: STAR DIVE' showcase.

These phenomena indicate that the game consumption structure of modern gamers has shifted from simple 'IP brand recognition' to 'operational sincerity and the speed of reflecting user feedback.' Consumers now consume not just the finished product, but the very process of a developer responding to user voices and improving the game, forming a psychological sense of belonging to the brand.

The era where past IP power guaranteed eternal profit is over; now, flexible updates and loyal community management are the lifeblood and capital of a game. As seen in the 1000% surge in concurrent players for 'Gray Zone Warfare' after an update, the ability to provide tangible changes that users can feel in a timely manner has become a core metric for survival on any platform. 📈

In the future market, success will be determined by fluid live service capabilities rather than static blockbusters. Is the game you love evolving in rhythm with its users, or is it stagnating by relying solely on past reputation? 🧐
— Dr. K
